event: Tiglath-pileser III campaign years (Philistia, Damascus)
quote: (734 BC) Bēl-dān | governor of Kalḫu (Nimrud) | to Philistia. (733 BC) Aššur-daʾʾinanni | governor of Mazāmua | to Damascus. (732 BC) Nabû-bēlu-uṣur | governor of Siʾme | to Damascus.
notes: Translit. 734: a-na KUR.pi-lis-ta; 733/732: a-na KUR.di-maš-qa. Entries for 725-723 (Shalmaneser V, Samaria years) are broken: 'to [...]'.

event: Gaza: Hanunu flees to Egypt, Gaza taken, Hanunu reinstated
quote: (As for) Ḫanūnu of the city Gaza, [who] fle[d before] my weapons [and] escaped [to] Egypt — [I conquered] the city Gaza, [his royal city, (and) I carried off] his property (and) [his] gods. ... Moreover, [as for him (Ḫanūnu), the terrifying splendor of (the god) Aššur, my lord over]whelmed him and he flew (back) [from Egypt] like a bird and [...]. I returned him to his position.
notes: Parallel Tigl. III 48 (Summ. 8, BM 131982) 14'b-19'b adds 800 talents of silver, his wife, sons, a stele at 'the city Brook of Egypt'; Tigl. III 49 rev. 13-16.

event: Damascus: Rezin besieged 45 days, orchards cut, 591 cities of 16 districts destroyed, deportations
quote: In order to save his life, he (Raḫiānu) fled alone and entered the gate of his city [like] a mongoose. I [im]paled his foremost men alive ... For forty-five days I set up my camp [aro]und his city and confined him (there) like a bird in a cage. I cut down his plantations, [...] ..., (and) orchards, which were without number; I did not leave a single one (standing). ... I carried off 800 people ... 750 captives from the cities Kuruṣṣâ (and) Samāya, (as well as) 550 captives from the city Metuna. Like tell(s) after the Deluge, I destroyed 591 cities of 16 districts of the land Damascus.
notes: No preserved Tiglath-pileser text states Rezin's death or capture; text breaks off. Annexation of Bīt-Ḫazā-il: Tigl. III 49 rev. 3.

event: Israel (Bīt-Ḫumrî): 16 districts, 13,520 captives
quote: [I utterly demolished ...] of sixteen dis[tricts of the land Bīt-Ḫumrî (Israel). I carried off (to Assyria) ...] capti[ves from ...], 226 [captives from ..., ...] captives [from ...], 400 [(and ...) captives from ...], 656 cap[tives from the city Sa..., ...] (altogether) 13,520 [people, ...], with their belongings.
notes: Place names and most numbers partly restored.

event: Israel: people deported; Pekah removed, Hoshea installed; tribute
quote: (As for) the land Bīt-Ḫumrî (Israel), I brought [to] Assyria [..., its "au]xiliary [army" ...] (and) all of its people, [...]. [I/they] killed Peqah, their king, and I placed Hoshea [as king o]ver them. I received from them ten talents of gold, ... talents of silver, [together with] their [proper]ty, and [I brou]ght them [to Assyria].
notes: Verb for Pekah damaged: {m}pa-qa-ḫa LUGAL-šú-nu [x]-du-x-x-ma; RINAP renders '[I/they] killed', not 'overthrew'. Summ. 9 rev. 10-11: '[... (and) I placed Hoshea as] king over them. [They brought ... to the city] Sarrabānu, before me' (Hoshea restored). 42:5'b-7': Gilead and Abil-šiṭṭi annexed.

event: Tribute list naming Jehoahaz (Ahaz) of Judah
quote: [... I received the paymen]t of Kuštašpi of the land Kummuḫu ... Sanīpu of the land Bīt-Ammon, Salāmānu of the land Moab, ...[... of ..., ... of ..., Mi]tinti of the land Ashkelon, Jehoahaz of the land Judah, Qauš-malaka of the land Edom, Muṣ...[... of ..., ... of ..., (and) Ḫa]nūnu of the city Gaza: gold, silver, tin, iron, lead, multi-colored garments, linen garments ...
notes: Translit. rev. 11': {m}ia-ú-ḫa-zi KUR.ia-ú-da-a-a. No year given for this payment.

event: Shalmaneser V ravages Samaria
source: Babylonian Chronicle ABC 1 (BM 92502 + dup., livius after Grayson)
quote: On the twenty-fifth of the month Tebêtu, Šalmaneser in Assyria and Akkad ascended the throne. He ravaged Samaria. The fifth year: Šalmaneser went to his destiny in the month Tebêtu.
notes: No year within the reign given; Samaria = Šamara'in in the chronicle.

event: Sargon II: Samaria conquered, 27,290 deported, 50 chariots
quote: I surrounded (and) conquered the city Samaria. I carried off as booty 27,290 of its inhabitants, conscripted fifty chariots from among them, and allowed the remainder to practice their (normal) occupations. I set a eunuch of mine over them and imposed upon them (the same) tribute (as) the former king (had paid).
notes: Translit. 24: 27 LIM 2 ME 90. Annals Room II (Sargon 1) 12b-17 'at the beginning of my reign' has the number fully restored. No Sargon text names Hoshea.

event: Sargon II: Samaria, deportees, resettlement
quote: (As for) the people of [(the city) Sa]maria who had [altogeth]er come to an agreement with a king [hostile to] me ... I foug[ht] them [and] counted [as] booty 47,280 people, together with [their] chariots and the gods who helped them. I conscripted two hundred chariots ... and settled the remainder of them in Assyria. I restored the city Samaria and made (it) greater than before. I brought there people from the lands that I had conquered. I set a eunuch of mine as provincial governor over them and considered them as people of Assyria.
notes: Numeral iv 31: [20?]+27 LIM 2 ME 80 (first element restored).

event: Battle of Raphia: Hanunu of Gaza and Re'e of Egypt defeated
quote: Ḫanūnu (Hanno), king of the city Gaza, with Rēʾe, the field marshal of Egypt, rose up to do war and battle against me at the city Rapḫia. I brought about their defeat. Rēʾe took fright at the clangor of my weapons and fled; his whereabouts have never been discovered. I captured Hanūnu, king of the city Gaza. || Annals: I captured [Ḫ]anūnu (Ḫanno) and brought him in bondage to my city Aššur; I then destroyed, demolished, (and) burned down with fire [the city Rap]ḫia. I carried off as booty 9,033 people ...
notes: Annals narrate it after the palû-2 heading (line 23b). Tang-i Var 22-24 and Sargon 8 also mention Raphia.

event: Ashdod: Iamani flees to Egypt/Meluhha, extradited; Sargon marches in person
quote: Furiously, I neither assembled the main force of my army nor organized my (military) camp. I marched to the city Ashdod with (only) my warriors who never leave my side ... that Iāmānī heard from afar of the approach of my expeditionary force and fled to the (far) edge of Egypt, on the border with the land Meluḫḫa ... I surrounded (and) conquered the cities Ashdod, Gath (and) Ashdod-Yam. ... The king of the land Meluḫ[ḫa] ... threw him (Iāmānī) in manacles and handcu[ffs], (in other words in) iron [fe]tters, and they brou[ght] (him) the long journey to Assyria, into my presence.
notes: No Sargon text mentions the turtānu at Ashdod. Nineveh Prism vii 13': 'In my ninth regnal year I marched to [the city Ashdod...]'; Annals place it under palû 11. Nineveh Prism vii 25''-32'': Philistia, Judah, Edom, Moab incited; gifts to Pirʾû king of Egypt. Eponym Chronicle 712: '(The king stayed) in the land' (i-na KUR); 711: 'Against the city Marqasa'.

event: Tang-i Var: Shapataku' (Shebitko) of Meluhha extradites Iamani
quote: I plundered the city Ashdod. Iāmānī, its king, took fright at my [weapon]s and abandoned his city. He fled to the border of the land Meluḫḫa and lived (there) stealthfully (lit.: "like a thief"). Šapatakuʾ (Shebitko), king of the land Meluḫḫa, heard of the mig[ht] of the gods Aššur, Nabû, (and) Marduk ... He put (Iāmānī) in handcuffs and manacles ... he had him [brou]ght in bondage [in]to my presence.
notes: Translit. 20: {m}šá-pa-ta-ku-⸢uʾ MAN⸣ KUR.me-luḫ-ḫa.

event: Sennacherib: battle of Eltekeh, Egyptian and Kushite charioteers and princes captured alive
quote: They formed a confederation with the kings of Egypt (and) the archers, chariots, (and) horses of the king of the land Meluḫḫa, forces without number, and they came to their aid. In the plain of the city Eltekeh, they sharpened their weapons while drawing up in battleline before me. ... I fought with them and defeated them. In the thick of battle, I captured alive the Egyptian charioteers (and) princes (lit. "the sons of the kings"), together with the charioteers of the king of the land Meluḫḫa.
notes: Rassam colophon: Ayyāru, eponymy of Mitūnu (700).

event: Sennacherib: 46 Judean cities taken by ramps and rams; 200,150 people
quote: (As for) Hezekiah of the land Judah, I surrounded (and) conquered forty-six of his fortified walled cities and small(er) settlements in their environs, which were without number, by having ramps trodden down and battering rams brought up, the assault of foot soldiers, sapping, breaching, and siege engines. I brought out of them 200,150 people, young (and) old, male and female, horses, mules, donkeys, camels, oxen, and sheep and goats, which were without number, and I counted (them) as booty.
notes: Ramps (šuk-bu-us a-ram-me) are tied to the 46 cities, not Jerusalem.

event: Sennacherib: Hezekiah confined in Jerusalem 'like a bird in a cage'; blockades
quote: As for him (Hezekiah), I confined him inside the city Jerusalem, his royal city, like a bird in a cage. I set up blockades against him and made him dread exiting his city gate. I detached from his land the cities of his that I had plundered and I gave (them) to Mitinti, the king of the city Ashdod, and Padî, the king of the city Ekron, (and) Ṣilli-Bēl, the king of the land Gaza, (and thereby) made his land smaller.
notes: Translit. 52: URU.ḪAL.ṢU.MEŠ UGU-šú ú-rak-kis-ma a-ṣe-e KÁ.GAL URU-šú ú-ter-ra ik-ki-bu-uš. Lemma search of all RINAP 3 texts naming Jerusalem/Hezekiah: no claim of entering/capturing Jerusalem and no siege ramp against it.

event: Sennacherib: Hezekiah's tribute sent to Nineveh after the campaign
quote: As for him, Hezekiah, fear of my lordly brilliance overwhelmed him and, after my (departure), he had the auxiliary forces (and) his elite troops whom he had brought inside to strengthen the city Jerusalem, his royal city, ... (along with) 30 talents of gold, 800 talents of silver, choice antimony ... together with his daughters, his palace women, male singers, (and) female singers brought into Nineveh, my capital city, and he sent a mounted messenger of his to me to deliver (this) payment and to do obeisance.
notes: Other summaries: Senn. 34:15 'I ruined the wide district of the land Judah (and) imposed my yoke on Hezekiah, its king'; Senn. 44:20b; Lachish epigraph Senn. 66 (BM 124911).

event: Sennacherib killed by his son
quote: On the twentieth day of the month Tebêtu, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, was killed by his son in a rebellion. For twenty-four years Sennacherib ruled Assyria. After the twentieth day of the month Tebêtu the rebellion continued in Assyria until the second day of the month Addaru. On the eighteenth day of the month Addaru Esarhaddon, his son, ascended the throne in Assyria.
notes: The son is not named.

event: Esarhaddon's account of his brothers' revolt
quote: Afterwards, my brothers went out of their minds and did everything that is displeasing to the gods and mankind, and they plotted evil, girt (their) weapons, and in Nineveh, without the gods, they butted each other like kids for (the right to) exercise kingship. ... In Addaru (XII), a favorable month, on the eighth day ... I joyfully entered Nineveh, my capital city, and I sat happily on the throne of my father. ... I sought out every one of the guilty soldiers, who wrongly incited my brothers to exercise kingship over Assyria, and imposed a grievous punishment on them: I exterminated their offspring.
notes: Does not mention the murder of Sennacherib or name any brother; rebels 'fled to an unknown land' (i 82-83).

event: Letter: 'Your son Arda-Mullissi will kill you'
quote: "It is about Arda-[Mullissi]." Th[ey covered] his face with his cloak and made him stand before Arda-Mul[lissi himself], saying: "Look! [Your appeal] is being granted, say it with your own mouth!" He said: "Your son Arda-[Mullissi] will kill you." They uncovered [his] face, and after Arda-Mu[llissi] had interrogated him, th[ey] kil[led] hi[m] and his brothers.
notes: Name partly restored in each occurrence (ARAD—{d}NIN.[LÍL]); beginning and addressee lost; reports a denunciation, not the murder.

event: Esarhaddon takes Memphis; Taharqa's wife, crown prince Ush-Anahuru and children deported to Assyria
quote: (as for) the city of Memphis, his royal city, within half a day (and) by means of mines, breaches, (and) ladders, I besieged (it), conquered (it), demolished (it), destroyed (it), (and) burned (it) with fire. I carried off to Assyria his wife, his court ladies, Uš-Anaḫuru, his crown prince, and the rest of his sons (and) his daughters, his goods, his possessions, his horses, his oxen, (and) his sheep and goats, without number. I tore out the roots of Kush from Egypt.
notes: Nahr el-Kalb (Esarh. 103) 7b-15: entered Memphis; booty incl. gods of Taharqa, his wife, court ladies, Uš-Anaḫuru.

event: Chronicle: Memphis captured, king's son and brother taken
quote: In the month Nisannu the army of Assyria marched to Egypt ... On the third, sixteenth and eighteenth days of the month Du'uzu - three times - there was a massacre in Egypt. ... On the twenty-second day Memphis, the royal city, was captured and abandoned by its king [Taharqo]. The king's son and brother were taken prisoner. The city was sacked, its inhabitants plundered, and its booty carried off.
notes: ABC 14:28-29 briefer.

event: Ashurbanipal's first and second Egyptian campaigns; sack of Thebes
quote: Tanutamon ... abandoned the city Thebes; he fled to the city Kipkipi. ... I conquered that city (Thebes) in its entirety. Silver, gold, precious stones, as much property of his palace as there was, garment(s) with multi-colored trim, linen garments, large horses, people — male and female — two tall obelisks cast with shiny zaḫalû-metal, whose weight was 2,500 talents ... I ripped (them) from where they were erected and took (them) to Assyria. I carried off substantial booty, (which was) without number, from inside the city Thebes.
notes: First campaign: Taharqa flees Memphis to Thebes; rebel kings brought to Nineveh (i 134b-ii 7). Prisms give campaign numbers, not years.

event: Marduk wrote 70 years of abandonment for Babylon, reversed to 11
quote: The merciful god Marduk [w]rote that the calculated time of its abandonment (should last) 70 years, (but) his heart was quickly soothed, and he reversed the numbers and (thus) ordered its (re)occupation to be (after) 11 years.
notes: Translit. ii 2-9: 70 MU.AN.NA.MEŠ mi-nu-ut ni-du-ti-šu iš-ṭur-ma ... e-liš a-na šap-liš uš-bal-kit-ma a-na 11 MU.AN.NA.MEŠ a-šab-šú iq-bi. Esarh. 116 (K 192): 'As the seventy years [passed, ...] he wrote [‘11 years’]'. Destroyer not named.

event: Fall of Nineveh: 3-month siege, booty, city turned to ruin heap; Cyaxares
source: Fall of Nineveh Chronicle ABC 3 (BM 21901; livius after Grayson)
quote: In the month Simanu, the Nth day, they encamped against Nineveh. From the month Simanu until the month Âbu - for three months - they subjected the city to a heavy siege. On the Nth day of the month Âbu they inflicted a major defeat upon a great people. At that time Sin-šar-iškun, king of Assyria, died. They carried off the vast booty of the city and the temple and turned the city into a ruin heap ... On the twentieth day of the month Ulûlu Cyaxares and his army went home.
notes: ANET 304-305: 'the king of the Manda-hordes (Umman-manda)'; Cyaxares = U-ma-kiš-tar; Sîn-šar-iškun clause damaged (ANET restores 'fled'); 'The city [they turned] into ruin-hills and hea[ps (of debris)]'.

event: Assur taken by the Medes; Nabopolassar-Cyaxares alliance
quote: In the month Âbu the Medes, after they had matched against Nineveh [lacuna], hastened and they captured Tarbisu ... encamped against Aššur. They did battle against the city and destroyed it. ... The king of Akkad and Cyaxares met one another by the city and together they made an entente cordiale.
notes: Livius renders Umman-manda as 'Medes'.

event: Harran taken from Aššur-uballiṭ and Egypt; failed counter-attack
quote: Fear of the enemy overcame Aššur-uballit and the army of Egypt that had come to help him, and they abandoned the city, and crossed the Euphrates. The king of Akkad reached Harran, fought a battle, and captured the city. He carried off the vast booty of the city and the temple. ... [yr 17] Aššur-uballit, king of Assyria, with a large army from Egypt crossed the river Euphrates and marched against Harran ... Until the month Ulûlu they did battle against the city but achieved nothing.

event: Carchemish: Egyptian army destroyed; Hamath
quote: Nebuchadnezzar his eldest son, the crown-prince, mustered the Babylonian army ... marched to Karchemiš which is on the bank of the Euphrates, and crossed the river to go against the Egyptian army which lay in Karchemiš. They fought with each other and the Egyptian army withdrew before him. He accomplished their defeat and beat them to non-existence. ... in the district of Hamath the Babylonian troops overtook and defeated them so that not a single man escaped to his own country.

event: Ashkelon captured, king seized, plundered, turned into mound and ruins
quote: He marched to the city of Aškelon and captured it in the month of Kislîmu. He captured its king and plundered it and carried off spoil from it. He turned the city into a mound and heaps of ruins and then in the month of Šabatu he marched back to Babylon.

event: Raid on the Arabs in the desert
quote: From the Hatti-land he sent out his companies, and scouring the desert they took much plunder from the Arabs, their possessions, animals and gods. In the month of Addaru the king returned to his own land.

event: 'City of Judah' taken 2 Addaru, king captured, king of his choice appointed, tribute
quote: In the seventh year, the month of Kislîmu, the king of Akkad mustered his troops, marched to the Hatti-land, and besieged the city of Judah and on the second day of the month of Addaru he seized the city and captured the king. He appointed there a king of his own choice, received its heavy tribute and sent to Babylon.
notes: ANET: 'laid siege to the city of Judah (Ia-a-hu-du) and the king took the city on the second day of the month Addaru. He appointed in it a (new) king of his liking'. Jerusalem, Jehoiachin, Zedekiah not named.

event: Oil rations for Ya'ukin king of Judah and his sons
date_bce: Nbk yr 13 (592/591) for Bab 28178; archive yrs 10-35
source: Weidner 1939 texts, transl. Oppenheim ANET 308; catalogue CDLI / Pedersén SPAB 2025
quote: 28122: ... t[o?] Ia-'-ú-kin, king ... || 28178: 10 (sila of oil) to ... [Ia]-'-kin, king of Ia[...]; 2½ sila (oil) to [... so]ns of the king of Judah (Ia-a-hu-du); 4 sila to 8 men from Judah (amēl Ia-a-hu-da-a-a) || 28186: 10 (sila) to Ia-ku-ú-ki-nu, the son of the king of Ia-ku-du (i.e. Judah); 2½ sila for the 5 sons of the king of Judah (Ia-ku-du) through Qana'a [...]
notes: Bab 28122 = SPAB 379 (CDLI P532837); Bab 28178 = VAT 16283+... = SPAB 360 (P532818), dated Nbk 13.XII; Bab 28186 = VAT 16378+17206 = SPAB 371 (P532829). Fractions OCR-garbled in archive.org text.

event: Nebuchadnezzar year 37 marches against Egypt (Amasis)
quote: ... [in] the 37th year, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Bab[ylon] mar[ched against] Egypt (Mi-ṣir) to deliver a battle. [Ama]sis (text: [...]-a(?)-su) of Egypt, [called up his a]rm[y] ... [...]ku from the town Puṭu-Iaman ... distant regions which (are situated on islands) amidst the sea ... [car]rying weapons, horses and [chariot]s ... he called up to assist him
notes: CDLI: BM 33041 = 1878-10-15,22+37; Wiseman, Chronicles 94-95; date Nbk 37. Outcome not preserved; Amasis restored.

event: Astyages captured by his army and handed to Cyrus; Ecbatana plundered
quote: [The sixth year: Astyages] mustered (his army) and marched against Cyrus, king of Anšan, for conquest [...] The army rebelled against Astyages and he was taken prisoner. Th[ey handed him over] to Cyrus. Cyrus <marched> to Ecbatana, the royal city. The silver, gold, goods, property, [...] which he carried off as booty (from) Ecbatana, he took to Anšan.
notes: ANET: 'King Ishtumegu'.

event: Cyrus crosses Tigris, marches to a land (Lydia?), kills its king
quote: In the month Nisanu, Cyrus, king of Parsu, mustered his army and crossed the Tigris below Arbela. In the month Ajaru, he marched to the land of... He killed its king, took his possessions, (and) stationed his own garrison (there) [...]
notes: Toponym broken; ANET restores 'Ly[dia]'; livius notes the reading is uncertain.

event: Nabonidus's western campaign: Edom (or Adummu); king in Tayma
quote: ABC 7: In the month Kislimu, the king [mustered] his army and to Nabû-tat-tan-úsur ... of Amurru to ... they/he encamped [against E]dom. || ii 5: The king (was) in Tayma (while) the prince, his officers, (and) his army (were) in Akkad. || Harran stele: for ten years, I walked the road between the cities Tēmā, Dadānu, Padakku, Ḫibrā, Yadīḫu, and (then) as far Yatribu. I did not enter my city, Babylon.
notes: ANET 305 reads '[Against the town A]dummu'. Sela' rock relief (RIBo Nabonidus 55) has only '(During my) fifth year [...] the kings of ...' and 'I am Nabonidus, king of Babylon'; no Edom legible.

event: Opis, Sippar, Babylon taken without battle; Ugbaru, Gubaru; gods returned
quote: When Cyrus did battle at Opis on the [bank of] the Tigris against the army of Akkad, the people of Akkad retreated. He carried off the plunder (and) slaughtered the people. On the fourteenth day Sippar was captured without a battle. Nabonidus fled. On the sixteenth day, Ugbaru, governor of Gutium, and the army of Cyrus, without battle they entered Babylon. ... On the third day of the month Arahsamna, Cyrus entered Babylon. ... Gubaru, his district officer, appointed the district officers in Babylon. From the month Kislimu to the month Addaru, the gods of Akkad which Nabonidus had brought to Babylon returned to their places. On the night of the eleventh of the month Arahsamna, Ugbaru died.
notes: ANET has 'In the month of Tashritu' at the start of iii 12 (omitted in livius). iii 8-12: gods of Marad, Kish, Hursagkalamma entered Babylon; those of Borsippa, Cutha, Sippar did not.

event: Cyrus Cylinder: entry into Babylon without battle; gods and peoples returned
source: RIBo Cyrus II 01 (Cyrus Cylinder, BM 90920 etc.)
quote: Without a fight or battle, he allowed him to enter Šuanna (Babylon). He saved his city, Babylon, from hardship. He delivered Nabonidus, the king who did not revere him, into his hands. ... From [Šuanna (Babylon)] to Aššur and Susa, Agade, Ešnunna, Zabbān, Mê-Turān, Dēr, as far as the border of the land of the Gutians, (and) cult-centers on the opposite side of the Tigris River whose dwellings had previous been in ruins — I returned the deities who live inside them to their (proper) places ... I gathered (together) all of their people and returned (them to) their settlements.
notes: Translit. 17: ba-lu qab-li ù ta-ḫa-zi ú-še-ri-ba-áš qé-reb šu-an-na.KI. No western place, Judah, Jerusalem or Jews named.

event: Kings of Tyre, Gaza, Sidon, Arwad, Ashdod at Nebuchadnezzar's court
source: RIBo Nebuchadnezzar II 011 (prism Ist EŞ 7834); ANET 307-308
quote: The king of Ty[re]; the king of Gaz[a]; the king of Sido[n]; the king of Arwa[d]; the king of Ashd[od]; the king of Mir[...]; (and) the king of [...].
notes: No king of Judah in the list (ANET n. 11). No siege of Tyre mentioned.

event: Men from Tyre on Babylonian ration lists; documents written at Tyre
quote: ... for 126 men from Tyre ...
notes: Joannès, 'Trois textes de Ṣurru à l'époque néo-babylonienne', RA 81 (1987) 147-158 (bibliography only). No cuneiform account of a Babylonian siege of Tyre found.

event: Citizens of Babylon go out to Seleucia (Antiochus I)
source: Astronomical Diary AD -273 B (BM 36710+92688+92689; ADART I; CDLI P364454)
quote: Year 37, (kings) Antiochus and Seleucus, month XII, the 9th, the satrap of Babylonia and the appointees of the king, who had gone before the king to Sardis in year 36, returned to Seleucia, the royal city which is on the Tigris. Their message (written on a) leather (scroll) came to the citizens of Babylon. The 12th day, the citizens of Babylon went out to Seleucia. That month, the satrap of Babylonia <...> the fields which had been given in year 32 at the command of the king for sustenance of the people of Babylon, Borsippa and Cutha.
notes: Translit. rev. 36': LU₂.DUMU.MEŠ E.KI ana URU.se-lu-ku-ʾa-a E₃.MEŠ. Same year: bricks molded for reconstruction of Esangila. Does not say Babylon was depopulated.

event: Latest datable cuneiform tablets (publication data)
text_id_and_lines: Sachs, Kramer AV (AOAT 25) 379-398; Hunger & de Jong, ZA 104/2 (2014) 182-194, doi:10.1515/za-2014-0015
notes: W22340a is from Uruk (Arsacid Era 326 = 79/80 CE). Latest diary on ORACC: AD -60 (Babylon). Specific Babylon 1st-c. CE tablets not verified (ADART VII not on ORACC).
